content.text: The verifier's narrative confirms every substantive element of the finding, and the only failing item is a sub-check that cannot be satisfied without a non-solicit clause existing. I won't manufacture one — inserting a solicitation restriction (with a carve-out) into an agreement that currently has none would create a covenant binding our own client where none was bargained for. That is precisely the outcome the rule's preferred position avoids. So the classification stands; I'll make the unmeasurability explicit in the rationale.

input.quote: (c) The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicit, no-hire or inducement covenant binds the Customer anywhere in this agreement, and no redline is proposed. I read the entire document (single "Preamble" section, p0000-p0074) and swept it: "solicit" and "induce" return zero hits; every "hire", "employ" and "personnel" hit is unrelated - indemnity for acts of third parties "hired by, employed, retained or under" a party's control (p0051, p0052), employee-directed confidentiality handling (p0056, p0061), independent-contractor status (p0066), and database access limited to "authorized personnel" (p0035, p0045). General Provisions (p0063-p0073) cover governing law, publicity, independent contractor status, notices, severability/survival, force majeure and assignment, and the survival list in p0070 (confidentiality, proprietary rights, indemnification, limitations of liability, effects of termination, governing law) contains no restrictive covenant. On the repeated "general-solicitation carve-out present" sub-check: a carve-out is a limitation on a restriction, so it is logically unmeasurable where no restriction exists. The only way to make that check pass would be to insert a non-solicit clause plus carve-out, which would impose a new restrictive covenant on our own client that the parties never bargained for - a materially worse outcome than the current silence and contrary to the rule's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"). I am therefore not treating the failed sub-check as a defect and am holding the compliant classification. Retained as internal evidence: if the Vendor introduces a non-solicit on redraft, accept no more than the fallback - mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and no no-hire.
